Revised assessment: Moderately positive but cautious. The hike to 1.25–1.50% alongside “gradual” guidance and a “symmetric” 2% goal is consistent with rule-like, inertial policy behavior documented by Clarida, Galí, and Gertler (2000) and with inflation-forecast–based frameworks (Svensson and Woodford, 2005). Persistent below-target inflation and two dovish dissents (Evans, Kashkari) temper the tone, aligning with concerns in the literature about tightening amid subdued price pressures and the transmission of higher rates through credit and cost channels to investment and inflation (Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans, 2005; Ravenna and Walsh, 2006). Implementation via IOER/RRP within a corridor remains accommodative (Goodfriend, 2002), reinforcing a cautious, gradualist stance.

Key sentence: “In view of realized and expected labor market conditions and inflation, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate… The Committee will carefully monitor actual and expected inflation developments relative to its symmetric inflation goal.”

Score: 0.58
